decisions.reason: As a floor-level shower drainage system it remains closely aligned with the firm's announced move toward low-profile and accessible bathroom solutions, so prior investment and strategic fit still argue for retention despite weaker recent visibility.

Because this designer shower drainage line was presented as a flagship for the firm's direction, the public commitment and need to justify that positioning make management very reluctant to withdraw it.

The shower element with integrated slope supports installation ease and renovation applications central to the firm's offer, so management would usually continue backing it and explain any weaker uptake as temporary.

Although less central than the shower-focused lines, it was launched prominently as a technical solution and a German drainage specialist would typically persist longer with such an invested, credibility-relevant product.

This air-admittance valve sits furthest from the firm's core shower-drainage narrative and had the weakest visible commitment, so by 2022 management is most likely to stop extending support and reallocate resources.
